product: Tirzepatide is the engine, sold as Mounjaro (9.943B in Q2 2026, up 91 pct) and Zepbound (4.928B, up 46 pct). Also Foundayo (orforglipron) oral GLP-1, Onswik weekly insulin, retatrutide triple agonist, plus Jaypirca, Ebglyss, Kisunla, Omvoh, Inluriyo and Verzenio. Key Products revenue reached 15.7B.
demand: Demand is the strongest line in the story. Volume grew 60 pct worldwide, total revenue 22.974B, and Q2 non-GAAP EPS of 8.38 beat the 6.40 consensus. Management said Lilly captures roughly 70 pct of new seniors entering the Medicare GLP-1 coverage program and about one-third of new oral GLP-1 patients.
pricing_power: Pricing power is weakening. Realized prices fell 13 pct worldwide, 36 pct ex-US after Mounjaro joined China NRDL, and US price fell about 9 pct excluding rebate and discount estimate adjustments. Zepbound cash-pay price cuts were an explicit driver. Higher gross margin came from mix and production cost, not price.
competition: Novo Nordisk remains the primary rival with CagriSema data; Viking Therapeutics VK2735 showed weight maintenance on less frequent dosing; Amgen and Pfizer are developing oral and monthly obesity options. Management acknowledges an increasingly crowded obesity market, though Lilly argues scale, oral Foundayo and the retatrutide data package defend its position.
team: David A. Ricks is chair and chief executive and framed Q2 as momentum plus pipeline building. Mike Czapar handles investor relations and Megan MacCauley media. Reported insider selling in August 2026 by EVP Anat Hakim and CAO Donald Zakrowski is the only team-related signal I could date from the sources read.
market_strategy: Volume-first global expansion funded by very large domestic manufacturing investment: an added 4.5B across Indiana sites and a 6.5B Houston plant for oral GLP-1 active ingredient. Lilly pairs this with aggressive business development, including Centessa, Kelonia, Orna, Ajax, AtaiBeckley, three infectious-disease deals and the InnoCare pact, plus Medicare Part D access expansion.
bull: Q2 2026 revenue 22.974B up 48 pct, non-GAAP EPS 8.38 beat 6.40 consensus, FY guidance raised to 85-87B; volume plus 60 pct, gross margin 85.8 pct; 13 of 13 analyst actions 90d were raises (Guggenheim 1273->1284, Cantor 1350->1410).
bear: Realized prices fell 13 pct worldwide, 36 pct ex-US; GAAP EPS midpoint cut 3.03 for acquired IPR&D; tax rate 23.3 pct vs 16.5 pct; insiders Hakim and Zakrowski sold ~7000 shares Aug 2026; crowded obesity market with Novo, Viking, Amgen.
falsifier: Q3 2026 earnings on 2026-10-29 (unconfirmed) showing worldwide realized price decline worse than Q2's 13 pct while volume growth falls below 40 pct, or FY2026 revenue guidance cut below 85B.
web_what_changed: 2026-08-05 Q2 2026: revenue 22.974B up 48 pct, non-GAAP EPS 8.38; FY2026 revenue guidance raised to 85-87B. Completed Orna, Ajax, Centessa and Kelonia acquisitions, signed AtaiBeckley deal, added three infectious-disease deals. Committed 4.5B more Indiana capex and broke ground on a 6.5B Houston plant. Retatrutide Phase 3 package complete.
web_not_known_yesterday: On 2026-09-24 the FDA approved Onswik, a once-weekly basal insulin for type 2 diabetes, and granted full approval to Inluriyo (imlunestrant) plus Verzenio in ESR1-mutated breast cancer. Lilly signed an InnoCare research and licensing deal worth up to 3.35B with 100M upfront. Read via aggregators and Reuters headlines only, not company or SEC pages.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Almost entirely volume. Q2 2026 worldwide volume rose 60 pct while realized prices fell 13 pct; US volume plus 37 pct with price minus 3 pct, ex-US volume plus 113 pct with price minus 36 pct after China NRDL inclusion. Gross margin still rose to 85.8 pct on favorable mix and production cost, so demand-led with real price erosion.
web_suppliers: not found. Nothing on suppliers or contract manufacturers appears in the Q2 2026 earnings release or the 8-K filings I read; Lilly instead emphasizes in-house capacity, with 4.5B of added Indiana investment and a 6.5B Houston active-ingredient plant. Constraint status of third-party suppliers is not disclosed in these sources.
web_customers: not found. No customer concentration is disclosed in the sources read. Lilly reports by geography and product rather than by customer. US revenue rose 33 pct to 14.4B and non-US revenue rose 80 pct to 8.6B, with Medicare Part D coverage cited as a driver of new senior GLP-1 starts, implying government and payer channels matter.
web_who_loses: Novo Nordisk loses share in incretins; Viking Therapeutics, Amgen and Pfizer face a scale disadvantage and pricing pressure; makers of daily basal insulin lose injections to Onswik; smaller obesity biotech competes for partner economics. Payers and patients ultimately fund the volume. Insurers and PBMs lose leverage as coverage expands.
web_contradicting_evidence: Realized prices fell 13 pct worldwide and 36 pct ex-US; US price minus 3 pct, or about minus 9 pct excluding rebate true-ups. GAAP EPS guidance midpoint was cut by 3.03 of acquired IPR&D, and the effective tax rate jumped to 23.3 pct from 16.5 pct. Insiders Anat Hakim and Donald Zakrowski sold about 7000 shares in August 2026; competitive data from Viking and Novo Nordisk pressure the multiple.
web_if_management_right: FY2026 revenue lands at 85-87B with non-GAAP EPS of 35.50-36.50, volume keeps compounding above 40 pct, new Indiana and Houston capacity removes supply ceilings, Foundayo scales in oral GLP-1 and Medicare, and a retatrutide BLA is filed to the FDA in Q1 2027, extending the franchise into sleep apnea and knee osteoarthritis.
web_if_management_wrong: Price erosion outruns volume. Government and NRDL pricing in China and Medicare cash-pay cuts compress realized prices faster than new patients arrive, oral and monthly GLP-1 entrants split the market, retatrutide slips or reimbursement narrows, and heavy capex plus recurring acquired IPR&D charges squeeze EPS and cash flow while the premium multiple de-rates.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Peptide and sterile fill-finish CDMOs, injectable device and pen makers, active-ingredient and cold-chain logistics providers, weight-management clinics and telehealth, and diagnostics for obesity and metabolic disease. Partner InnoCare receives 100M upfront plus milestones. Construction and engineering firms benefit from the 6.5B Houston and Indiana buildout.
